subject: Islamic Studies
q: The first revealed verses of the Qur’an belong to Surah:
explanation: The opening verses of Surah Al-Alaq, beginning “Iqra” (Read), were the first to be revealed in the Cave of Hira.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Qur’an was revealed over a period of about:
explanation: Revelation began in the Cave of Hira and continued until shortly before the Prophet’s (PBUH) death, about 13 years in Makkah and 10 in Madinah.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: According to Surah Al-Qadr, the Qur’an was sent down in:
explanation: Surah Al-Qadr opens: “Indeed, We sent it down in the Night of Decree.”

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Hazrat Uthman (RA) ordered that the standard copies of the Qur’an be written in the dialect of:
explanation: Uthman (RA) instructed the committee that, where they differed, they should write in the dialect of the Quraysh, in which the Qur’an had been revealed.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The compilation of the Qur’an into one volume under Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) was prompted by the martyrdom of many Huffaz in the Battle of:
explanation: Many memorisers of the Qur’an were martyred at Yamamah against Musaylimah, so Umar (RA) urged Abu Bakr (RA) to have the Qur’an collected.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Whom did Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) entrust with collecting the Qur’an into a single compiled copy?
explanation: Zaid bin Thabit (RA), a chief scribe of revelation, gathered the Qur’an from written materials and the memories of Companions.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Which Caliph is known as ‘Jami-ul-Qur’an’ for sending standard copies of the Qur’an to different provinces?
explanation: To end differences in recitation, Uthman (RA) had standard copies prepared from Abu Bakr’s compilation and sent them to the major cities.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The compiled copy of the Qur’an prepared under Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) was later kept in the custody of:
explanation: The copy passed from Abu Bakr (RA) to Umar (RA) and then to his daughter Hafsa (RA), from whom Uthman (RA) borrowed it.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Under which Caliph was the Qur’an first compiled into a single volume after the death of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
explanation: The first compilation in book form (mushaf) was made in the caliphate of Abu Bakr (RA); Uthman (RA) later standardised its copies.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The systematic addition of dots and vowel marks to the Qur’anic script is associated with the governorship of:
explanation: As non-Arabs entered Islam, Hajjaj bin Yusuf, the Umayyad governor of Iraq, had scholars add dots and marks to prevent errors in recitation.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Surahs revealed before the Hijrah are called:
explanation: Surahs revealed before the migration to Madinah are termed Makki, and those revealed after it Madani.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Which is a characteristic feature of Madani Surahs?
o: Short, rhythmic verses stressing the Hereafter
Addressing only the idolaters of Makkah
Detailed laws on family, society, war and economy
explanation: In Madinah a Muslim society and state took shape, so Madani Surahs contain detailed legal and social injunctions.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: In the sciences of the Qur’an, ‘Naskh’ means:
o: Abrogation of a ruling by a later ruling
explanation: Naskh is the replacement of an earlier legal ruling by a later one, as in the gradual prohibition of wine.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: ‘Asbab al-Nuzul’ refers to:
o: The occasions or circumstances of revelation
explanation: Knowing the background in which verses were revealed helps in understanding their meaning and application.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The explanation and interpretation of the Qur’an is called:
explanation: Tafsir means to explain or unveil; it is the science of interpreting the meanings of the Qur’an.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: ‘Tajweed’ refers to:
o: The rules for correct recitation of the Qur’an
explanation: Tajweed literally means “to make good”; it governs the correct pronunciation and articulation of the Qur’anic text.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Verses of the Qur’an whose meaning is clear and decisive are called:
explanation: Surah Aal-e-Imran describes the Muhkamat as the foundation of the Book, while the Mutashabihat are verses open to more than one meaning.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: ‘Huruf-e-Muqatta‘at’ are:
o: Disjointed letters at the beginning of some Surahs
explanation: Letters such as Alif-Lam-Mim open several Surahs; their exact meaning is known to Allah.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Ayat-ul-Kursi is part of Surah:
explanation: Ayat-ul-Kursi, which describes Allah’s knowledge and sovereignty, is in Surah Al-Baqarah.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Which Surah is called ‘Umm-ul-Kitab’ (the Mother of the Book)?
explanation: Al-Fatiha sums up the essential themes of the Qur’an and is recited in every rak‘ah of Salah, hence Umm-ul-Kitab.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Which Surah is popularly called the ‘Heart of the Qur’an’?
explanation: A narration in Tirmidhi calls Surah Yasin the heart of the Qur’an; it stresses Tawhid, prophethood and resurrection.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Which Surah is popularly known as ‘Arus-ul-Qur’an’ (the Bride of the Qur’an)?
explanation: Surah Ar-Rahman, with its refrain “Which of the favours of your Lord will you deny?”, is traditionally called the Bride of the Qur’an.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Which Surah does not begin with Bismillah?
explanation: Surah At-Tawbah is the only Surah that does not open with Bismillah-ir-Rahman-ir-Rahim.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: In which Surah does Bismillah occur twice?
explanation: Besides its opening, Bismillah appears within Surah An-Naml at the start of Hazrat Sulaiman’s (AS) letter to the Queen of Sheba.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The only Surah named after a woman is:
explanation: Surah Maryam bears the name of the mother of Hazrat Isa (AS), the only woman mentioned by name in the Qur’an.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) said that Surah Al-Ikhlas is equal to:
explanation: According to Sahih al-Bukhari, Surah Al-Ikhlas is equivalent to a third of the Qur’an because it sums up pure Tawhid.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Which Surah is a concise declaration of the Oneness of Allah?
explanation: Al-Ikhlas declares that Allah is One, Self-Sufficient, neither begetting nor begotten, with none comparable to Him.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Surah Al-Falaq and Surah An-Nas are together called:
explanation: Both begin “Say: I seek refuge…”, so they are called the Mu‘awwidhatayn, the two Surahs of seeking refuge.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Which two Surahs are called ‘Az-Zahrawayn’ (the two radiant ones) in a Hadith?
explanation: Sahih Muslim reports the Prophet (PBUH) urging believers to recite the two radiant ones, Al-Baqarah and Aal-e-Imran.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) said that which Surah and its sister Surahs had made his hair grey?
explanation: In a narration in Tirmidhi the Prophet (PBUH) said “Hud and its sisters have made me grey”, referring to their stern warnings about the Hereafter and the fate of nations.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Which Surah narrates in one continuous account what the Qur’an calls ‘the best of stories’ (Ahsan-ul-Qasas)?
explanation: Surah Yusuf opens by calling its narrative the best of stories and relates the life of Hazrat Yusuf (AS) from beginning to end.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The story of the Ashab-e-Kahf (People of the Cave) is narrated in Surah:
explanation: Surah Al-Kahf relates how young believers took refuge in a cave and were made to sleep for many years.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The advice of a wise man to his son about Tawhid, prayer and good manners is recorded in Surah:
explanation: Surah Luqman contains Luqman’s counsel to his son: avoid Shirk, honour parents, pray, be patient and humble.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Which Surah is noted for its guidance on social conduct, forbidding ridicule, suspicion and backbiting?
explanation: Surah Al-Hujurat lays down manners of brotherhood, verification of news and the prohibition of mockery, suspicion and backbiting.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The verses clearing Hazrat Aisha (RA) of the slander (Ifk) were revealed in Surah:
explanation: Surah An-Nur declared Aisha (RA) innocent and laid down the law on false accusation of unchastity.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The detailed shares of inheritance are laid down mainly in Surah:
explanation: The fixed shares of heirs are set out in Surah An-Nisa, which deals extensively with family law.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The rules for distributing the spoils of war (Mal-e-Ghanimah) are given in Surah:
explanation: Surah Al-Anfal, revealed after Badr, takes its name from “the spoils” and fixes the one-fifth share and its recipients.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Surah Al-Ma’idah takes its name from:
o: The feast of the Farewell Hajj
The table spread sent down at the request of the disciples of Hazrat Isa (AS)
The food of the people of Paradise
explanation: Near its end the Surah relates the disciples asking Hazrat Isa (AS) for a table spread with food from heaven.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Surah Al-Fil refers to the destruction of:
explanation: Surah Al-Fil recalls how Allah destroyed Abraha’s elephant-led army that came to demolish the Ka‘bah.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Which short Surah states that mankind is in loss except those who believe, do good deeds, and urge one another to truth and patience?
explanation: Imam Shafi‘i remarked that if people reflected on Surah Al-Asr alone it would suffice them, as it sums up the way to success.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Which Surah condemns those who repulse the orphan, neglect their prayers and refuse small kindnesses?
explanation: Surah Al-Ma‘un links true faith with care for the orphan and the needy and sincere, attentive prayer.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Which Surah is named after a metal?
explanation: Al-Hadid means iron; the Surah mentions that Allah sent down iron with great strength and benefits for mankind.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Surah An-Nahl is named after:
explanation: An-Nahl means the bee; the Surah describes the bee and the healing honey it produces. The ant is An-Naml and the spider Al-Ankabut.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) is called ‘Khatam-an-Nabiyyin’ (Seal of the Prophets) in Surah:
explanation: Surah Al-Ahzab states that Muhammad (PBUH) is the Messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Which of the following is the longest Surah of the Holy Qur’an?
explanation: Al-Baqarah is the longest Surah of the Qur’an; An-Nisa and Aal-e-Imran are also long but shorter.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The shortest Surah of the Holy Qur’an is:
explanation: Al-Kawthar, with three very short verses, is the shortest Surah of the Qur’an in length.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The longest verse of the Holy Qur’an, which deals with writing down debts, is known as:
explanation: The verse of debt (Ayat-ud-Dayn or Mudayana) in Surah Al-Baqarah instructs that loan transactions be recorded before witnesses.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: What is ‘Rabbi Zidni Ilma’ (My Lord, increase me in knowledge)?
explanation: This prayer is part of a verse of Surah Ta-Ha in which the Prophet (PBUH) is taught to ask for more knowledge.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Which name of the Qur’an means ‘the Criterion between truth and falsehood’?
explanation: Al-Furqan means that which distinguishes right from wrong; Surah Al-Furqan opens with this name of the Qur’an.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The word ‘Qur’an’ literally means:
o: That which is read or recited
explanation: Qur’an comes from qara’a (to read, to recite), so it means the oft-recited book.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Qur’anic promise ‘Indeed, We sent down the Reminder and indeed We will be its guardian’ refers to:
o: The preservation of the Qur’an by Allah
The safety of the Prophet (PBUH) in Makkah
The victory of the believers at Badr
explanation: In Surah Al-Hijr Allah Himself guarantees the preservation of the Qur’an (Adh-Dhikr) from change.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Surah Al-Ma’idah describes the Qur’an as ‘Muhaymin’ over earlier scriptures, meaning it is:
o: A guardian and criterion over them
explanation: Muhaymin means a watcher and guardian: the Qur’an confirms what is true in earlier scriptures and judges over them.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Qur’an’s challenge to its opponents to produce a Surah like it is known as:
explanation: In several Surahs the Qur’an challenges doubters to bring even one Surah like it; this challenge is called Tahaddi.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: ‘I‘jaz-ul-Qur’an’ refers to:
explanation: I‘jaz means rendering others incapable: the Qur’an’s language and content cannot be matched by any human work.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The recognised modes of reciting the Qur’an, transmitted from the Prophet (PBUH), are called:
explanation: Qira’at are the authentic variant readings of the Qur’an handed down through reliable chains of reciters.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Ma‘arif-ul-Qur’an, a widely read Urdu Tafsir, was written by:
explanation: Mufti Muhammad Shafi, the first Grand Mufti of Pakistan, wrote the eight-volume Tafsir Ma‘arif-ul-Qur’an.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Tafhim-ul-Qur’an was written by:
explanation: Maulana Maududi wrote Tafhim-ul-Qur’an, a six-volume Urdu translation and commentary completed in 1972.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Tadabbur-e-Qur’an, noted for its emphasis on the coherence (nazm) of the Qur’an, was written by:
explanation: Amin Ahsan Islahi developed the idea of thematic coherence taught by his teacher Hamiduddin Farahi in Tadabbur-e-Qur’an.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Zia-ul-Qur’an, a Tafsir in Urdu, is the work of:
explanation: Pir Muhammad Karam Shah al-Azhari of Bhera, also a judge of the Shariat Appellate Bench, wrote Zia-ul-Qur’an.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The classical Tafsir ‘Jami‘ al-Bayan’ was written by:
explanation: Ibn Jarir al-Tabari’s Jami‘ al-Bayan, known as Tafsir al-Tabari, is the foundational tafsir based on narrations.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Tafsir al-Jalalayn is so called because it was written by:
o: Two brothers of the Jalal family
A scholar and his royal patron Jalal
Two teachers of Jalal al-Din Rumi
Two scholars who were both named Jalal al-Din
explanation: It was begun by Jalal al-Din al-Mahalli and completed by his student Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti, hence “the two Jalals”.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Tarjuman-ul-Qur’an, an Urdu translation and commentary, was written by:
explanation: Maulana Abul Kalam Azad wrote Tarjuman-ul-Qur’an; its introduction on Surah Al-Fatiha is especially celebrated.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Shah Abdul Qadir, son of Shah Waliullah, is known for:
o: His Urdu translation of the Qur’an, Mudih-ul-Qur’an
explanation: Shah Abdul Qadir’s Mudih-ul-Qur’an and his brother Shah Rafi-ud-Din’s literal version were among the earliest Urdu translations.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: ‘The Holy Qur’an: Text, Translation and Commentary’, a famous English translation, is the work of:
explanation: Abdullah Yusuf Ali’s translation with commentary appeared in the 1930s; Pickthall’s was titled “The Meaning of the Glorious Koran”.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Reciting ‘A‘udhu billahi min ash-shaitan ir-rajim’ before reading the Qur’an is called:
explanation: The Qur’an commands seeking refuge with Allah from Satan before recitation; this is Ta‘awwudh, while Tasmiyah is saying Bismillah.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Al-Lawh al-Mahfuz, mentioned in Surah Al-Buruj, is:
o: The first written copy of the Qur’an
explanation: Surah Al-Buruj says the glorious Qur’an is inscribed in a Preserved Tablet (Lawh-e-Mahfuz) with Allah.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Which Surah foretold the victory of the Romans over the Persians after their defeat?
explanation: Surah Ar-Rum opens by announcing that the defeated Romans would be victorious within a few years, which came to pass.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Night Journey (Isra) of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) is mentioned at the beginning of Surah:
explanation: Surah Al-Isra begins by glorifying Allah who took His servant by night from Masjid-ul-Haram to Masjid-ul-Aqsa.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Surah Al-Mujadilah opens with the complaint of a woman whose husband had pronounced:
explanation: Khawlah bint Tha‘labah pleaded about her husband’s Zihar, and the opening verses of Al-Mujadilah abolished it as a form of divorce and prescribed expiation.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Which Surah is also known as Surah Bara’ah?
explanation: At-Tawbah opens with “Bara’ah” (a declaration of disassociation) from the idolaters who broke their treaties, hence its second name.
